assets/audio/banh-chung-banh-giay/page-0.text: Long ago, the sixth Hùng King wanted to choose which son would be king after him.
He said, “Bring a gift for our ancestors at Tết, and the most meaningful gift will win.”
The princes searched far and wide for rare treasures from the forests and the sea.
But the youngest prince, Lang Liêu, was poor and lived simply, growing rice.
Lang Liêu worried, “I have no treasures, so what can I give?”
One night, a kind spirit came to him in a dream.
“Nothing is more precious than rice,” said the spirit.
“Use it to make your gift.”
Lang Liêu wrapped sticky rice, green beans, and pork in green leaves to make a square cake.
Then he pounded sticky rice into a soft, round, white cake.
On Tết, the king tasted every gift and smiled at the two simple cakes.
“The square cake is like the earth, and the round cake is like the sky,” Lang Liêu explained.
The king was moved and said, “These cakes show love for our land and thanks to our parents.”
He chose Lang Liêu to be the next king.
Ever since, Vietnamese families make bánh chưng and bánh giầy for Tết.
They share them together, giving thanks for rice, family, and home.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-01/sentence-01.text: Once upon a time, two brothers lived in a quiet village.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-01/sentence-02.text: When they grew up, the older brother took the big house and the rice fields.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-01/sentence-03.text: The younger brother kept only a small hut and an old star fruit tree.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-02/sentence-01.text: The younger brother cared for the tree every day, and it grew sweet, golden fruit.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-02/sentence-02.text: One morning, a huge, beautiful bird flew down and began to eat the star fruit.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-03/sentence-01.text: “Dear bird, this tree is all I have,” the younger brother said softly.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-03/sentence-02.text: The bird answered, “Eat one fruit, pay back with gold. Sew a bag three hands long to carry it home.”

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-04/sentence-01.text: The younger brother sewed a small bag, just as the bird said.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-04/sentence-02.text: The bird carried him over the sea to an island that sparkled with gold.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-04/sentence-03.text: He filled his little bag, thanked the bird, and flew home happily.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-05/sentence-01.text: He used the gold to help poor neighbors and to build a cozy home.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-05/sentence-02.text: The older brother heard the story and asked to trade his big house for the star fruit tree.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-06/sentence-01.text: When the bird came, the older brother sewed a bag that was much too big.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-06/sentence-02.text: On the island, he stuffed it so full of gold that the bird could hardly fly.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-07/sentence-01.text: “Your bag is too heavy,” said the bird. “Please let some gold go.”

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-07/sentence-02.text: The older brother opened his hands, and the gold dropped into the sea.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-07/sentence-03.text: The bird brought him safely home, and his heart felt lighter.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-08/sentence-01.text: From then on, the two brothers shared what they had and cared for the star fruit tree together.

assets/audio/cay-khe/page-08/sentence-02.text: And the sweet star fruit was always enough for everyone.

assets/audio/chu-cuoi/page-01/sentence-0.text: Long ago, a kind woodcutter named Cuội lived at the edge of a green forest.
Every morning, he walked into the woods with his axe and a happy song.

assets/audio/chu-cuoi/page-02/sentence-0.text: One day, Cuội saw a little tiger cub with a sore paw.
Soon the mother tiger came and laid some banyan leaves on the cub's paw.
In a moment, the cub was well again and ran off to play.

assets/audio/chu-cuoi/page-03/sentence-0.text: Cuội was amazed, so he carefully dug up the little banyan tree and carried it home.
He planted it beside his house, and its leaves helped many sick neighbors feel better.

assets/audio/chu-cuoi/page-04/sentence-0.text: The banyan tree was magical, so it needed special care.
Cuội told his wife, “Please water it only with clean, fresh water.”

assets/audio/chu-cuoi/page-05/sentence-0.text: One evening, while Cuội was still in the forest, his wife forgot and used water from the muddy pond.
Suddenly, the banyan tree began to sway, and its roots lifted out of the ground.

assets/audio/chu-cuoi/page-06/sentence-0.text: Cuội came running home just as the tree floated up into the sky.
He held on to a root, and up, up, up they went, all the way to the moon.

assets/audio/chu-cuoi/page-07/sentence-0.text: Now Cuội sits under the banyan tree on the moon, caring for it every night.
When you look at the full moon, you might see a tree with a little man beneath it.

assets/audio/chu-cuoi/page-08/sentence-0.text: At the Mid-Autumn Festival, children carry glowing lanterns to send their love up to Cuội.

assets/audio/coc-kien-troi/page-01/sente.text: Long ago, there was a long, dry summer with no rain at all.
The rivers were empty, and the plants and animals were very thirsty.

assets/audio/coc-kien-troi/page-02/sente.text: A little toad said, “Let's go up to the sky and ask the Jade Emperor for rain.”
Along the way, a crab, a bear, a tiger, some bees, and a fox came along too.

assets/audio/coc-kien-troi/page-03/sente.text: When they reached the sky palace, the toad bravely beat the big drum.
Boom, boom, boom! The sound echoed through the clouds.

assets/audio/coc-kien-troi/page-04/sente.text: The Thunder God came out grumbling, but the bees buzzed and the friends stood close together.
Seeing them so united, the Thunder God took them to see the Jade Emperor.

assets/audio/coc-kien-troi/page-05/sente.text: The little toad bowed and said, “Your Majesty, the earth has had no rain for so long.”
“The plants are dry, and the animals are thirsty, so please send us rain.”

assets/audio/coc-kien-troi/page-06/sente.text: The Jade Emperor was surprised that such a small toad was so brave.
He called the Rain God, and soon cool rain began to fall.

assets/audio/coc-kien-troi/page-07/sente.text: “From now on,” said the Jade Emperor, “when the toad grinds his teeth, I will send rain.”
The friends cheered and hurried home through the falling rain.

assets/audio/coc-kien-troi/page-08/sente.text: The rivers filled up, and the fields turned green again.
That is why people say, “The toad is the Sky's uncle.”

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-01/sentence-01.text: Long ago, the land was troubled, and people longed for peace.

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-01/sentence-02.text: The Dragon King who lived beneath the waters decided to lend them a magic sword.

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-02/sentence-01.text: A fisherman named Lê Thận cast his net and pulled up a shiny blade.

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-02/sentence-02.text: On it were two words, Thuận Thiên, which mean “following Heaven.”

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-03/sentence-01.text: Later, the leader Lê Lợi saw a strange light shining in a banyan tree.

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-03/sentence-02.text: There he found a jeweled sword handle, and it fit the blade perfectly.

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-04/sentence-01.text: With the magic sword, Lê Lợi and his friends grew brave and strong.

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-04/sentence-02.text: Together, they brought peace back to the land.

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-05/sentence-01.text: One sunny day, King Lê Lợi went boating on Tả Vọng Lake.

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-05/sentence-02.text: Suddenly, a great Golden Turtle rose from the water.

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-06/sentence-01.text: “The Dragon King lent you his sword,” said the turtle. “Now that there is peace, please give it back.”

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-06/sentence-02.text: The king smiled and gently held out the sword.

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-07/sentence-01.text: The turtle took the sword in its mouth and dove down into the deep, quiet water.

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-07/sentence-02.text: A soft glow shimmered on the lake for a long time.

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-08/sentence-01.text: From then on, the lake was called Hồ Gươm, the Lake of the Returned Sword.

assets/audio/ho-guom/page-08/sentence-02.text: It still sits in the heart of Hà Nội, calm and green, reminding us to cherish peace.

assets/audio/mai-an-tiem/page-01/sentenc.text: Long ago, a young man named Mai An Tiêm lived at the king's palace.
He believed that everything we have comes from our own hard work.

assets/audio/mai-an-tiem/page-02/sentenc.text: The king did not like these words, so he sent An Tiêm and his family to a faraway island.
The island had only sand, rocks, and the wide blue sea.

assets/audio/mai-an-tiem/page-03/sentenc.text: An Tiêm did not give up, so he built a little hut and caught fish to eat.
His wife and children gathered shells and planted small gardens.

assets/audio/mai-an-tiem/page-04/sentenc.text: One day, a flock of birds flew by and dropped some black seeds on the sand.
An Tiêm thought, “If the birds can eat it, people can eat it too.”

assets/audio/mai-an-tiem/page-05/sentenc.text: He planted the seeds and watered them every day.
Soon, long green vines grew big round fruits with dark green stripes.

assets/audio/mai-an-tiem/page-06/sentenc.text: Inside, the fruit was bright red, juicy, and sweet.
They called it dưa hấu, the watermelon.

assets/audio/mai-an-tiem/page-07/sentenc.text: An Tiêm carved his name on some melons and set them floating on the sea.
Sailors found them and came to the island to trade rice and cloth for watermelons.

assets/audio/mai-an-tiem/page-08/sentenc.text: When the king heard the story, he understood and welcomed An Tiêm's family home.
And that is how the sweet watermelon came to Vietnam.

assets/audio/nang-tien-oc/page-01/senten.text: Long ago, a poor old woman lived alone beside a lotus pond.
Every day she caught snails and crabs to sell at the market.
One dawn, she found a little snail whose shell shimmered like green jade.

assets/audio/nang-tien-oc/page-02/senten.text: “You are too lovely to sell,” she said, and she placed it in the water jar at home.
Every day she gave it fresh water and talked to it softly.

assets/audio/nang-tien-oc/page-03/senten.text: From then on, something wonderful happened whenever she came home.
The floor was swept, the garden was watered, and warm rice waited on the tray.

assets/audio/nang-tien-oc/page-04/senten.text: One morning, she pretended to go out, then tiptoed back and hid behind the door.
She watched as a lovely young woman stepped out of the snail shell.

assets/audio/nang-tien-oc/page-05/senten.text: The fairy swept the floor, cooked the rice and hummed a gentle song.
The old woman crept to the jar and tucked the empty shell safely away.

assets/audio/nang-tien-oc/page-06/senten.text: Then she hugged the fairy and said, “Please stay with me, my dear daughter.”
The fairy smiled, and she stayed.

assets/audio/nang-tien-oc/page-07/senten.text: From then on, the two of them lived happily together, caring for each other as mother and daughter.
And every summer, the lotus pond bloomed pink outside their door.

assets/audio/qua-va-binh-nuoc/page-01/se.text: On a hot summer day, a thirsty crow flew over a sunny stone path.
He looked everywhere for water, but every puddle had dried up.

assets/audio/qua-va-binh-nuoc/page-02/se.text: At last, he spotted a tall clay pitcher beside a garden wall.
But the water was right at the bottom, and his beak could not reach it.

assets/audio/qua-va-binh-nuoc/page-03/se.text: Crow tried to tip the pitcher over, but it was far too heavy.
So he sat on the wall and thought very hard.

assets/audio/qua-va-binh-nuoc/page-04/se.text: Then he noticed the little pebbles scattered along the path.
He picked one up in his beak and dropped it into the pitcher. Plink!

assets/audio/qua-va-binh-nuoc/page-05/se.text: One pebble, two pebbles, ten pebbles, twenty.
With every pebble, the water rose a little higher.

assets/audio/qua-va-binh-nuoc/page-06/se.text: At last, the cool water reached the top, and Crow drank and drank.
He fluffed his feathers and cawed a happy thank-you to the little pebbles.

assets/audio/rua-va-tho/page-01/sentence.text: In a bright green woodland lived a hare who loved to boast about how fast he could run.
“No one is quicker than me!” he said, bouncing in circles.

assets/audio/rua-va-tho/page-02/sentence.text: Tortoise smiled slowly. “Shall we have a race?”
Hare laughed so hard that both his ears flopped down.

assets/audio/rua-va-tho/page-03/sentence.text: Squirrel drew a starting line, and all the woodland animals gathered to watch.
“Ready, set, go!” Hare zoomed away, and Tortoise took one small step.

assets/audio/rua-va-tho/page-04/sentence.text: Halfway along, Hare looked back and could not even see Tortoise.
“I have time for a nap,” he yawned, and he lay down under a shady tree.

assets/audio/rua-va-tho/page-05/sentence.text: Tortoise kept walking, step by step, across the brook and up the hill.
Even when his legs felt tired, he did not stop.

assets/audio/rua-va-tho/page-06/sentence.text: When Hare woke up, the sun was low, and he dashed toward the finish.
But Tortoise was already crossing the line as the animals cheered.

assets/audio/rua-va-tho/page-07/sentence.text: Hare’s ears drooped. “You were slow, but you never gave up,” he said.
Tortoise smiled, and the two friends walked home together, nice and slow.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-01/sentence-01-.text: Long ago, a kind old couple lived beside the rice fields.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-01/sentence-02-.text: They longed for a child, and one day a baby boy arrived, snug and round inside a coconut shell.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-01/sentence-03-.text: His mother hugged him close and named him Sọ Dừa.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-02/sentence-01-.text: When Sọ Dừa grew bigger, he asked to herd goats for the rich man of the village.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-02/sentence-02-.text: Everyone laughed, but every evening his goats came home round, full and happy.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-03/sentence-01-.text: The rich man had three daughters, and they took turns bringing Sọ Dừa his lunch.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-03/sentence-02-.text: The two older sisters wrinkled their noses, but the youngest always spoke to him kindly.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-04/sentence-01-.text: One noon, the youngest sister heard sweet flute music drifting down from the hill.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-04/sentence-02-.text: She saw a gentle young man playing under a tree, but when she came closer, only Sọ Dừa was there.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-05/sentence-01-.text: Sọ Dừa asked his mother to tell the rich man that he wished to marry.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-05/sentence-02-.text: The rich man asked for a jar of gold, ten rolls of silk and ten fat pigs, sure it could never be done.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-05/sentence-03-.text: On the wedding day, every gift was there, laid out neatly in the yard.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-06/sentence-01-.text: The older sisters turned away, but the youngest smiled and said, “I will marry him.”

assets/audio/so-dua/page-06/sentence-02-.text: At the wedding feast, Sọ Dừa stepped out of his shell as a handsome young man.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-06/sentence-03-.text: Everyone gasped, and then the whole village cheered.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-07/sentence-01-.text: Sọ Dừa studied day and night by the light of a little oil lamp.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-07/sentence-02-.text: He came first in the royal exam and became a wise official who cared for the people.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-08/sentence-01-.text: The two older sisters felt ashamed of how they had laughed at him.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-08/sentence-02-.text: Sọ Dừa forgave them with a smile.

assets/audio/so-dua/page-08/sentence-03-.text: And the village remembered the youngest sister’s kind heart for a long, long time.

assets/audio/son-tinh-thuy-tinh/page-01/.text: Long ago, the eighteenth Hùng King had a lovely daughter named Mỵ Nương.
Two mighty spirits came to ask to marry her.

assets/audio/son-tinh-thuy-tinh/page-02/.text: Sơn Tinh, the Mountain Spirit, could raise hills with a wave of his hand.
Thủy Tinh, the Water Spirit, could call the rain and the wind.

assets/audio/son-tinh-thuy-tinh/page-03/.text: The king said, “Whoever brings the wedding gifts first may marry my daughter.”
He asked for an elephant with nine tusks, a rooster with nine spurs, and a horse with nine red manes.

assets/audio/son-tinh-thuy-tinh/page-04/.text: Early the next morning, Sơn Tinh arrived first with all the gifts.
He took Mỵ Nương home to his mountain.

assets/audio/son-tinh-thuy-tinh/page-05/.text: When Thủy Tinh arrived late, he was very upset.
He called the rain and the wind, and the river rose higher and higher.

assets/audio/son-tinh-thuy-tinh/page-06/.text: But Sơn Tinh calmly raised the hills even higher, one by one.
The villagers worked together, carrying earth and stones to keep their homes safe.

assets/audio/son-tinh-thuy-tinh/page-07/.text: At last, Thủy Tinh grew tired, and the water flowed slowly back to the sea.
The sun came out, and the rice fields turned green again.

assets/audio/son-tinh-thuy-tinh/page-08/.text: Some say Thủy Tinh still remembers, and that is why the rains come each summer.
And each year, people help one another stay safe, just like long ago.

assets/audio/su-tich-trau-cau/page-01/se.text: Long ago, two brothers named Tân and Lang looked so alike that even their neighbors mixed them up.
They went everywhere together, like two leaves on one branch.

assets/audio/su-tich-trau-cau/page-02/se.text: Tân, the older brother, married a kind young woman, and the three of them lived together.
But Tân was busier now, and Lang began to feel a little left out.

assets/audio/su-tich-trau-cau/page-03/se.text: One evening, the young wife greeted Lang as her husband, because the brothers looked so alike.
The house fell quiet, and Lang thought sadly, “Maybe I am in the way.”

assets/audio/su-tich-trau-cau/page-04/se.text: Lang quietly left home and walked until he reached a wide, rushing stream.
He sat on the bank, missing his brother, and waited so long that he became a smooth white stone.

assets/audio/su-tich-trau-cau/page-05/se.text: Tân missed his brother and set out to find him.
At the stream, he stood beside the white stone until he grew into a tall, slender areca palm.

assets/audio/su-tich-trau-cau/page-06/se.text: The young wife searched for her husband too.
When she found the palm, she wrapped her arms around it and became a green betel vine, winding gently upward.

assets/audio/su-tich-trau-cau/page-07/se.text: Years later, a kind king passed by and heard the story.
He folded a betel leaf around a slice of areca with a pinch of white lime, and it turned a warm red, like a loving heart.

assets/audio/su-tich-trau-cau/page-08/se.text: Since then, at Vietnamese weddings and at Tết, betel and areca are offered first, as a wish for love and togetherness.
As grandparents still say, “A betel leaf begins every conversation.”

assets/audio/su-tu-va-chuot/page-01/sent.text: On the golden savanna, a great lion lay sleeping in the warm sun.
A tiny mouse scampered by and ran right over his nose.

assets/audio/su-tu-va-chuot/page-02/sent.text: The lion woke up and caught the mouse under one big paw.
“Please let me go,” squeaked Mouse. “One day, I might help you.”

assets/audio/su-tu-va-chuot/page-03/sent.text: The lion chuckled. “How could someone so small ever help me?”
But he lifted his paw, and Mouse dashed away.

assets/audio/su-tu-va-chuot/page-04/sent.text: A few days later, the lion stepped into a hunter’s rope net.
He pulled and roared, but the ropes only held him tighter.

assets/audio/su-tu-va-chuot/page-05/sent.text: Mouse heard the roar and came running as fast as she could.
She nibbled and nibbled, snipping one rope after another.

assets/audio/su-tu-va-chuot/page-06/sent.text: Soon the lion stepped free and bowed his great head.
“Thank you, little friend,” he said. “Small can be mighty.”
From that day on, the lion and the mouse were the best of friends.

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-01/sentence-01.text: Long ago, there lived a gentle girl named Tấm and her stepsister, Cám.

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-01/sentence-02.text: Tấm worked hard all day, while Cám liked to play.

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-02/sentence-01.text: One day, their stepmother said, “Whoever catches the most fish will win a red silk top.”

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-02/sentence-02.text: Tấm filled her basket, but Cám tricked her and took the fish home.

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-03/sentence-01.text: Tấm sat by the pond and cried, and then a kind old fairy named Bụt appeared.

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-03/sentence-02.text: “Don't cry, my child,” said Bụt. “Look, one little goby fish is still in your basket.”

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-04/sentence-01.text: Tấm put the little fish in the well and shared her rice with it every day.

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-04/sentence-02.text: She sang, “Bống bống bang bang, come and eat my gold and silver rice.”

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-04/sentence-03.text: Later, Bụt helped the little fish swim off to the wide river, safe and free.

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-05/sentence-01.text: Soon the king held a grand festival, but the stepmother mixed two kinds of rice together for Tấm to sort.

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-05/sentence-02.text: Bụt sent a flock of little sparrows, and they sorted every grain.

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-06/sentence-01.text: Bụt also gave Tấm a lovely dress and a pair of embroidered slippers.

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-06/sentence-02.text: On the way to the festival, one slipper fell into the water, right where the king's elephant was passing.

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-07/sentence-01.text: The king picked up the tiny slipper and said, “Whoever this slipper fits will be my bride.”

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-07/sentence-02.text: Many girls tried it on, but it fit only Tấm's foot.

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-08/sentence-01.text: Tấm became queen and kept her kind and gentle heart.

assets/audio/tam-cam/page-08/sentence-02.text: She forgave Cám and her stepmother, and they learned to be kind, too.

assets/audio/thanh-giong/page-01/sentenc.text: In the village of Phù Đổng, an old couple had a little boy named Gióng.
Gióng was three years old, but he had not yet spoken a word.

assets/audio/thanh-giong/page-02/sentenc.text: One day, the king sent a messenger to find someone brave to protect the land.
Suddenly, Gióng spoke: “Mother, please invite the messenger in.”

assets/audio/thanh-giong/page-03/sentenc.text: Gióng told the messenger, “Please ask the king for an iron horse, an iron whip, and iron armor.”
The messenger hurried back to the palace with the news.

assets/audio/thanh-giong/page-04/sentenc.text: From then on, Gióng grew bigger and bigger every day.
The whole village shared rice and vegetables to help feed him.

assets/audio/thanh-giong/page-05/sentenc.text: When the iron horse arrived, Gióng stretched and stood up as tall as a tree.
He jumped on the horse, and it breathed out a bright, warm glow.

assets/audio/thanh-giong/page-06/sentenc.text: Gióng rode bravely and chased the invaders far away from the land.
When his iron whip broke, he pulled up tall bamboo to keep going.

assets/audio/thanh-giong/page-07/sentenc.text: When the land was peaceful again, Gióng rode up Sóc Sơn mountain.
He took off his armor, and he and his horse flew gently up into the sky.

assets/audio/thanh-giong/page-08/sentenc.text: People say the golden bamboo and the round ponds near the village were left by Gióng's horse.
And every spring, the village holds a festival to remember the brave boy.

assets/audio/tich-chu/page-01/sentence-0.text: Long ago, a little boy named Tích Chu lived with his loving grandmother.
Grandma gave Chu the best food and sang him to sleep every night.

assets/audio/tich-chu/page-02/sentence-0.text: As Chu grew bigger, he spent all day playing with his friends.
He forgot that Grandma was home alone.

assets/audio/tich-chu/page-03/sentence-0.text: One hot day, Grandma felt sick and very thirsty.
“Chu, please bring me some water,” she called softly, but Chu was far away playing.

assets/audio/tich-chu/page-04/sentence-0.text: Grandma turned into a little bird and flew out the window.
“Chu, Chu,” the bird sang as it flew toward the sky.

assets/audio/tich-chu/page-05/sentence-0.text: When Chu came home, he cried, “Grandma, please come back, and I will take care of you!”
A kind fairy appeared and said, “Bring her water from the spring on the far mountain.”

assets/audio/tich-chu/page-06/sentence-0.text: Chu walked through forests and climbed over hills without giving up.
At last, he found the sparkling spring and filled a little gourd.

assets/audio/tich-chu/page-07/sentence-0.text: Chu found the little bird and gently offered it the fresh water.
The bird drank, and right away, it became Grandma again.

assets/audio/tich-chu/page-08/sentence-0.text: Chu hugged Grandma tight and promised to always look after her.
